title: Microscopic Insights into the Role of High-Valence Elements in Stabilizing Nickel-Based Cathodes for High-Energy Batteries
content: Nickel-based layered oxides, such as LiNiO2 and its derivatives, are the preferred cathodes for lithium-ion batteries powering electric vehicles due to their high energy density. A critical challenge for their practical use is chemo-mechanical instability during electrochemical cycling, which is often mitigated by incorporating high-valence elements like niobium (Nb) during the calcination process [1-3]. However, the exact role of Nb remains unclear. Specifically, it has been unknown whether Nb is incorporated into the crystal lattice as a dopant or segregates at the boundaries as lithium niobate impurities, and how this affects crystal growth and defect formation during calcination, consequently influencing the resulting material properties. To address these questions, we employ scanning/transmission electron microscopy (S/TEM) combined with in situ synchrotron X-ray spectroscopy to investigate how Nb stabilizes Ni-based cathodes, focusing on LiNiO2 and LiNi₈3Mn₀₅Co₁2O2 (Ni83). This approach allows us to identify the spatial distribution of Nb in intermediates and the final products and to assess how Nb regulates calcination, thereby impacting chemo-mechanical and electrochemical properties of the synthesized cathodes.
